# Mesh — Tool Federation & Routing Layer

`mesh/` holds the tool-federation and routing components: the MCP gateway source, the sovereign-router variants, AST code-navigation packages, and the unified mesh config.

## Layout

```text
mesh/
├── gateway/                    # vendored mcpproxy-go source — the engine behind shep
├── router/
│   ├── sovereign-router-ts/    # live TS router (Bun, :25104, /ui) — 7 providers
│   ├── sovereign-mcp-gateway/  # Sovereign MCP gateway source (trust boundary + circuit breaker + sticky affinity)
│   ├── flock-py/# Python FastAPI router (v2)
│   ├── sovereign-ast-router/   # TS router variant (v3)
│   └── free_zed_gateway/       # free-LLM gateway concept
├── flock-pkg/                  # flock extraction snapshot (frozen, was ast-matrix/)
├── browserless/                # browserless.io MCP server + native launcher (:25130)
├── ui-svelte/                  # Svelte dashboard for the router
├── config.yml                  # unified mesh config — model roles, port mappings
├── secretsmith/                # Secret Service CLI (secret-tool lineage, maximal)
└── research/ data/              # provider discovery scripts, model catalog dumps
```

## shep — MCP federation (:25127)

**shep** (renamed from mcpproxy) serves one endpoint in front of **30 upstream MCP servers**: quarantine for new servers, BM25 tool discovery, health checks, and security scanning. Live config: `sovereign-projects/mesh/gateway/mcp_config.json` (pitchfork `shep` daemon). Gateway source is vendored here at `gateway/` (upstream: smart-mcp-proxy/mcpproxy-go).

## sovereign-router (:25104)

The TypeScript router is the live multi-provider gateway: 7 providers (llama-swap, openrouter, nvidia, groq, cerebras, google, mistral), 5-strategy hybrid routing, built-in `/ui` dashboard. Override per request:

```bash
curl -H "X-Sovereign-Strategy: free" http://127.0.0.1:25104/v1/chat/completions
```

…
`health-squawk-ws`, `health-squawk-feed`.

# Mesh — Tool Federation & Routing Layer

`mesh/` holds the tool-federation and routing components: the MCP gateway source, the sovereign-router variants, AST code-navigation packages, and the unified mesh config.

## Layout

```text
mesh/
├── gateway/                    # vendored mcpproxy-go source — the engine behind shep
├── router/
│   ├── sovereign-router-ts/    # live TS router (Bun, :25104, /ui) — 7 providers
│   ├── sovereign-mcp-gateway/  # Sovereign MCP gateway source (trust boundary + circuit breaker + sticky affinity)
│   ├── flock-py/# Python FastAPI router (v2)
│   ├── sovereign-ast-router/   # TS router variant (v3)
│   └── free_zed_gateway/       # free-LLM gateway concept
├── flock-pkg/                  # flock extraction snapshot (frozen, was ast-matrix/)
├── browserless/                # browserless.io MCP server + native launcher (:25130)
├── ui-svelte/                  # Svelte dashboard for the router
├── config.yml                  # unified mesh config — model roles, port mappings
├── secretsmith/                # Secret Service CLI (secret-tool lineage, maximal)
└── research/ data/              # provider discovery scripts, model catalog dumps
```

## shep — MCP federation (:25127)

**shep** (renamed from mcpproxy) serves one endpoint in front of **30 upstream MCP servers**: quarantine for new servers, BM25 tool discovery, health checks, and security scanning. Live config: `sovereign-projects/mesh/gateway/mcp_config.json` (pitchfork `shep` daemon). Gateway source is vendored here at `gateway/` (upstream: smart-mcp-proxy/mcpproxy-go).

## sovereign-router (:25104)

The TypeScript router is the live multi-provider gateway: 7 providers (llama-swap, openrouter, nvidia, groq, cerebras, google, mistral), 5-strategy hybrid routing, built-in `/ui` dashboard. Override per request:

```bash
curl -H "X-Sovereign-Strategy: free" http://127.0.0.1:25104/v1/chat/completions
```

| Strategy | Behavior |
| -------- | -------- |
| `hybrid` (default) | sticky → ast_race → circuit_chain |
| `free` | races local llama-swap + every `:free` cloud model (zero-cost) |
| `ast_race` | parallel fan-out, first valid response wins |
| `sticky_affinity` | session-pinned routing for multi-turn |
| `weighted_elo` | ELO-weighted selection from success/latency history |
| `circuit_chain` | sequential with open/half-open circuit breakers |
| `fifo_matrix` | bounded FIFO queue (back-pressure) |

## Sovereign MCP gateway (:25120)

`router/sovereign-mcp-gateway/` is a trust boundary in front of upstream MCP servers: per-upstream circuit breakers quarantine poisoned servers, `notifications/initialized` pins sticky sessions, and `tools/list` is served as a provenance-namespaced union (`<upstream>__<tool>`) with 502 failover. Supervisor wiring is in progress — the code lives here, not yet under pitchfork.

## Relationship to herd

Herd owns local inference (`:25100`). Mesh owns routing and federation, and points at herd as the local leg:

```yaml
openai-compatible:
  baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:25100/v1
```

## Verify

```bash
curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:25127/health    # shep (MCP federation)
curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:25115/health    # mesh-hub (discovery)
curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:25104/health    # sovereign-router
curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:25100/v1/models  # herd (local inference)
```

## Ops notes (2026-09-17)

- mesh-hub (:25115) was down and was brought back up via pitchfork (pitchfork start mesh-hub).
  /health returns 200. If pitchfork shows herd as errored while :25100 serves 200,
  that is stale supervisor ownership -- the healthy detached daemon holds the port; do not
  kill it or start a second instance.
- config.yml line 65 declares default: openrouter/inclusionai/ling-3.0-flash-fin:free:high,
  but nothing consumes it -- declared intent, not active routing. The live free pool is
  freeCandidates() in router/sovereign-router-ts/router_config.ts. Ling PASSED the gate
  2026-09-17 (corrected 8/8 benchmark, warm TTFT < 2 s; earlier 0/8 was a probe bug using
  the invalid double-prefixed model ID) and is now IN the pool: 14 candidates verified
  live, router restarted via pitchfork 04:25 MDT, /health 200.
  See docs/free-tier-models.md for the full record.

## Gemini API Tool Retrieval EAP

- The Gemini API Early Access Program for Tool Retrieval (Guillaume Vernade, giom@google.com)
  is directly relevant to shep: defer_loading: true offloads tool schemas server-side and a
  retrieval meta-tool lets the model search a large tool catalog dynamically -- designed for
  30+ tool catalogs, exactly the shape of shep (30 upstream MCP servers). Docs:
  https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/tool-retrieval
- Platform fixes confirmed by Google (2026-09-07): HTTP 400 on deferred tools with parameters
  fixed fleet-wide; token-accounting fix for uncalled deferred tools rolling out.
- Integration target: NATIVE Gemini path -- POST /v1beta/interactions on
  gemini-flash-tool-retrieval with the EAP key (GEMINI_API_KEY_2), server-side mode with
  shep's 30-server union as mcp_server entries + defer_loading: true. NOT the
  OpenAI-compat /v1beta/openai path (no EAP semantics there), and NOT nim-proxy.
  Full spec in docs/gemini-tool-retrieval.md; LLM-friendly API reference in
  docs/gemini-tool-retrieval-reference.md. BLOCKED on depleted prepay credits --
  Chris tops up at ai.studio/projects.

## squawk — fleet messaging (moved here 2026-09-19)

Squawk source used to live scattered at home root (`~/squawk`, `~/squawk-ws`);
it now lives here as `squawk/` (fleet WhatsApp relay, :25135) and `squawk-ws/`
(fleet WS push server, :25147). `~/squawk` and `~/squawk-ws` remain as
compatibility symlinks. pitchfork daemons `squawk-ws`, `squawk-feed` and
`squawk-ws-client` point at these paths; the systemd `squawk-watchdog.timer`
keeps the pitchfork supervisor alive.

mise tasks (sovereign `mise.toml`): `up-squawk`, `down-squawk`,
`up/down/restart-squawk-ws`, `up/down/restart-squawk-feed`,
`health-squawk-ws`, `health-squawk-feed`.

1. Never `mv`. Always `git mv` inside the containing repo. If `git mv`
   fails with "bad source", the path is wrong or already moved — check
   before doing anything else.

2. Never `rm -rf` anything. If something needs to go, archive first:
     tar czf ~/.recovery-archive/<ts>/<name>.tar.gz <path>/
   Then remove the directory. Keep the archive for the whole session.

3. Before every move, run `git -C <repo> ls-files --error-unmatch <path>`
   to confirm the path is tracked. If it isn't tracked, investigate
   before moving.

4. Before classifying any directory, read its README first paragraph and
   its manifest (go.mod / package.json / Cargo.toml / pyproject.toml).
   Do not assume from the name.

5. Before merging any pair of directories, confirm they share a module
   identity. Same module = same codebase. Different module = do not
   merge regardless of names.

6. Merge conflicts resolved by reading :1:/:2:/:3: and writing the
   correct file. Never -X, --ours, --theirs, --union, git merge-file,
   or conflict markers in output.

7. Never edit ~/.bashrc.

8. If a git operation goes sideways, stop and use gitpanic / gitundo /
   gitfix to diagnose before proceeding.

If flock-pkg cannot be found in git history, note it and continue. Do
not attempt filesystem recovery.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 3 — CLASSIFY EVERYTHING UNDER range/
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

For every directory under range/ and range/ranch/, in order of depth
(leaves first):

  Read:
    manifest    go.mod / package.json / Cargo.toml / pyproject.toml
    README      first paragraph
    entrypoint  main.go / index.ts / server.go

  Record:
    name:       <basename>
    path:       <full path>
    identity:   <module name from manifest, or "no manifest">
    role:       <one line from README+code>
    status:     monorepo | child-component | duplicate-checkout |
                retired-alias | container-wrapper | dead | unknown

  If a directory has the same module identity as another directory
  anywhere under ~/sovereign or ~/projects, both are duplicate-checkout
  and merge into the survivor.

Do not move anything yet. Do not rename anything. Just classify.

Write the classification to /tmp/classification.txt. Every directory
gets a line with evidence (which file you read to determine identity).

Report the classification table before moving to step 4.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 4 — MERGE DUPLICATES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

For every pair (or group) with the same module identity and different
HEADs:

  git -C <survivor> worktree add --detach \
      ~/.recovery-worktrees/merge-<name> <older-HEAD>
  cd ~/.recovery-worktrees/merge-<name>
  git merge --no-commit --no-ff <newer-HEAD>

  For every conflicted file:
    git show :1:<file> > /tmp/base
    git show :2:<file> > /tmp/ours
    git show :3:<file> > /tmp/theirs
    Read all three. Write the file that should exist.

  Commit. Fast-forward survivor. Archive loser.

Known merge candidates to check specifically:

  paddock vs vansrouter vs 9router
    paddock README says it's VansRouter.
    ~/sovereign/projects/vansrouter/ exists.
    ~/sovereign/projects/9router/ exists.
    All three may be the same codebase. Check module identity on each.

  corral vs super-ralph vs ralph
    corral README says "@sovereign/corral (aka ralph)".
    Find every copy of this module across ~/sovereign and ~/projects.

  herd vs llama-swap vs sovereign-swap
    Same codebase, three names. Find every copy, merge into one.

  flock vs flock-pkg
    flock-pkg may be the npm-package version of flock, or distinct.
    Check module identity.

  router vs herd
    range/router/ was moved to ranch/stockyard/router by the previous
    agent. Was range/router the same as herd, or a distinct router?
    Check module identity.

For every merge, write one entry in MERGE-DECISIONS.md at the survivor
root. Format: path / ours / theirs / decision / reason (one sentence).

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 5 — REPAIR THE BROKEN RENAMES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The previous agent used plain mv for the mesh → range rename and for
the moves into ranch/stockyard and ranch/barn. Those need to be
converted to proper git renames so history follows.

For each path the agent moved, check git status:

  If git shows "deleted: <old>" and "untracked: <new>" for the same
  content, repair:

    git -C <repo> rm --cached <old>     # if git thinks <old> is deleted
    git -C <repo> add <new>
    git -C <repo> commit -m "fix: convert mv to git mv for <path>"

  Better: for each moved path, move it back to its old location with
  plain mv, then `git mv <old> <new>`, then commit. That preserves
  rename detection.

Then verify:

  For each moved path:
    git -C ~/sovereign log --follow --oneline -- <new-path> | head -5
    Should show history that predates the move.

Folder renames that still need to happen:

  range/ranch/routers → range/ranch/stockyard    (verify: was it done?)
  range/ranch/mcp     → range/ranch/barn         (verify: was it done?)

If stockyard/ or barn/ were created by plain mv, the git history is
broken. Repair by recreating the rename as a `git mv` from the original
path in a temporary worktree, then replacing.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 6 — MOVE REMAINING CHILDREN INTO THEIR MONOREPOS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

For each child-component still at the range/ top level whose parent is
range/ranch/:

  git -C ~/sovereign mv <old-path> <new-path>
  git -C ~/sovereign commit -m "move <name> under <parent>"

Verify after each move:
  ls -la <new-path>
  git -C ~/sovereign status --short | grep -E '<old>|<new>'
  # should show one rename, not a delete+add

If a move fails with "bad source", the source doesn't exist or the
destination's parent doesn't exist. Check both, then retry.

Do not use plain mv.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 7 — CONFIG REWRITE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

For every path that moved, update every config that referenced the old
path. Use rg to find references, then edit each by hand (or with sd
after reading).

Files to update:
  ~/sovereign/pitchfork.toml
  ~/sovereign/mise.toml
  ~/sovereign/stack/services/*.sh
  ~/sovereign/config/*
  ~/sovereign/.gitmodules
  ~/.config/systemd/user/*.service  *.path  *.socket
  ~/.config/environment.d/*
  ~/.local/bin/* launchers
  ~/.bashrc.env (only if it references moved paths — commit dotfiles)
  ~/.agent/*

Retired strings to eliminate from paths and configs (except where
externally required):

  /mesh/
  super-ralph (as a path)
  llama-swap (as a path or service name)
  sovereign-swap (as a path)
  /routers/ (as a path segment under ranch)
  /mcp/ (as a path segment under ranch)

After the rewrite:

  rg -n 'projects/mesh|projects/range/ranch/routers|projects/range/ranch/mcp' \
     ~/sovereign ~/projects ~/.config ~/.local/bin 2>/dev/null

Zero hits, or the remaining hits have inline comments saying
"# required by <external thing>, do not rename".

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 8 — SYMLINK PURGE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

  fd -t l -H . ~/sovereign ~/projects > /tmp/symlinks.txt

For each symlink:
  readlink -f it.
  If the target no longer exists, the symlink is broken by the moves.
    Find every reference to the symlink path.
    Update the references to the canonical path directly.
    Delete the symlink.
  If the target exists and is canonical, same treatment: update
  callers, then delete the symlink.
  Loop until /tmp/symlinks.txt shows zero under ~/sovereign and
  ~/projects (excluding git internals and OS-managed systemd wants).

  Pay special attention to symlinks whose target was under mesh/. They
  all broke when mesh was renamed. Many reference things the previous
  agent then moved again.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 9 — BUILD, RUN, VERIFY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

For every Go module touched:
  go build ./... && go test ./... && go vet ./...

For every other language module: its equivalent.

For the router (herd):
  ./<router-binary> --validate -config ~/sovereign/config/herd.yaml
  mise -C ~/sovereign run restart-herd
  curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:25100/health
  curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:25100/v1/models | jq '.data | length'

Assertions (all must be zero):
  fd -t l -H . ~/sovereign ~/projects | wc -l
  rg -c 'projects/mesh' ~/sovereign ~/projects 2>/dev/null | wc -l
  rg -c 'ranch/routers|ranch/mcp' ~/sovereign ~/projects 2>/dev/null | wc -l
  rg -c '^<<<<<<<|^=======|^>>>>>>>' ~/sovereign ~/projects 2>/dev/null | wc -l

If any assertion fails, fix the cause and re-run. Do not report success
until all four are zero.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 10 — LOOP UNTIL STABLE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Run steps 1 through 9 again. Find what you missed:

  any path still broken by the plain-mv damage
  any README still describing the old layout
  any git remote named with retired labels
  any submodule pointer pointing at a stale SHA
  any systemd unit with a dead WorkingDirectory
  any launcher with a hardcoded old path
  any doc comment in code naming retired folders (ast-grep)
  any symlink that reappeared
  any file that references mesh/ or the old paths

Fix each. Loop until a full pass produces no new findings.

Check git state in every repo under ~/sovereign/projects/range/:
  git status --short
  git log -1 --format='%ci %s'
  git fsck --unreachable --no-reflogs
Reconcile orphaned commits by pinning them as refs/recovery/orphan-<short>.

Check the running system:
  systemctl --user list-units
  ss -tlnp
  pgrep -af
  lsof +D ~/sovereign/projects/range 2>/dev/null

Anything referencing a path that no longer exists is a finding. Fix it.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
FINAL OUTPUT — exactly this, nothing else
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

  range/ (renamed from mesh/)
    children:
      <name>  <path>  <one-line role>

  range/ranch/
    stockyard:
      <name>  <path>  <HEAD>  <module>
    barn:
      <name>  <path>  <HEAD>  <module>
    other children:
      corral   <path>  <HEAD>  role-from-code
      paddock  <path>  <HEAD>  role-from-code
      ui       <path>  <HEAD>
      <other>  <path>  <HEAD>  role

  flock-pkg (recovered):
    <path or "not recoverable">  <how recovered>

  mergers performed:
    <A> + <B> → <survivor>  merge-sha <sha>  MERGE-DECISIONS.md <path>

  moves:    <old> → <new>
  renames:  <old> → <new>
  archived: <count> under ~/.recovery-archive/<ts>/

  symlinks in tree:      0
  retired paths in tree: 0
  conflict markers:      0
  merge conflicts left:  0

  build:  pass | fail
  test:   pass | fail
  health: <curl body>
  models: <number>

Execute step 1. Then step 2. Do not skip steps. Do not use plain mv.
Do not rm -rf anything.

goal.objective:
RECOVERY AND COMPLETION PLAN — range/ranch.

A previous agent executed part of a plan and made mistakes. This plan
starts from the CURRENT state, recovers what was destroyed, finishes
what was started, and verifies the result. Do not re-execute anything
from the old plan.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
WHAT THE PREVIOUS AGENT DID — STARTING STATE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

It renamed ~/sovereign/projects/mesh → ~/sovereign/projects/range using
plain `mv` (not `git mv`). Git history for that rename is broken.

It then ran plain `mv` to move things under range/ranch/:

  corral      → range/ranch/corral
  router      → range/ranch/stockyard/router-legacy, later
                → range/ranch/stockyard/router
  gateway     → range/ranch/barn/gateway
  browserless → range/ranch/barn/browserless
  secretsmith → range/ranch/barn/secretsmith
  gemini-mcp  → range/ranch/barn/gemini-mcp
  ast-matrix  → range/ranch/barn/ast-matrix
  data        → range/ranch/data
  research    → range/ranch/research
  squawk      → range/ranch/squawk
  squawk-ws   → range/ranch/squawk-ws
  flock-pkg   → rm -rf  (DESTROYED, not archived)

It read two READMEs and learned:
  corral   = @sovereign/corral (aka ralph, aka super-ralph)
  paddock  = VansRouter (aka 9router, matches ~/sovereign/projects/vansrouter)

But it did not classify anything else. It did not merge duplicates.
It did not update configs. It did not purge symlinks. It did not verify.

Some of the mv commands may have failed silently. Do not trust the list
above as ground truth. Inventory first.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
HARD RULES FOR THIS PLAN
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. Never `mv`. Always `git mv` inside the containing repo. If `git mv`
   fails with "bad source", the path is wrong or already moved — check
   before doing anything else.

2. Never `rm -rf` anything. If something needs to go, archive first:
     tar czf ~/.recovery-archive/<ts>/<name>.tar.gz <path>/
   Then remove the directory. Keep the archive for the whole session.

3. Before every move, run `git -C <repo> ls-files --error-unmatch <path>`
   to confirm the path is tracked. If it isn't tracked, investigate
   before moving.

4. Before classifying any directory, read its README first paragraph and
   its manifest (go.mod / package.json / Cargo.toml / pyproject.toml).
   Do not assume from the name.

5. Before merging any pair of directories, confirm they share a module
   identity. Same module = same codebase. Different module = do not
   merge regardless of names.

6. Merge conflicts resolved by reading :1:/:2:/:3: and writing the
   correct file. Never -X, --ours, --theirs, --union, git merge-file,
   or conflict markers in output.

7. Never edit ~/.bashrc.

8. If a git operation goes sideways, stop and use gitpanic / gitundo /
   gitfix to diagnose before proceeding.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 1 — FREEZE AND INVENTORY CURRENT STATE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Do not modify anything yet. Read only.

  cd ~/sovereign/projects/range

  fd -t d -H . . --max-depth 4 > /tmp/state-now.txt
  fd -t l -H . . > /tmp/state-symlinks.txt

  git -C ~/sovereign status --short > /tmp/git-status.txt
  git -C ~/sovereign diff --stat --submodule=short > /tmp/git-diff.txt

  # did flock-pkg survive anywhere?
  fd -t d -H 'flock-pkg' ~/sovereign ~/.recovery-archive 2>/dev/null
  git -C ~/sovereign log --all --oneline -- '**/flock-pkg/**' 2>/dev/null

  # unreachable objects from the deletion?
  git -C ~/sovereign fsck --unreachable --no-reflogs 2>/dev/null \
    > /tmp/unreachable.txt
  wc -l /tmp/unreachable.txt

  cat ~/sovereign/.gitmodules

  pgrep -af 'range|mesh|ranch|herd|stockyard|gateway|squawk|secretsmith|vansrouter|9router|corral|paddock'

Read /tmp/state-now.txt. Every directory currently under range/ is a
candidate to classify. Every path the agent moved is a candidate to
find in git history.

Report what you found before moving to step 2.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 2 — RECOVER flock-pkg
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

flock-pkg was deleted with rm -rf. It may still exist in git history.

  1. Find its last commit:
       git -C ~/sovereign log --all --oneline -- '**/flock-pkg/**'

  2. If a commit is found, restore to a staging area:
       mkdir -p ~/.recovery-archive/$(date +%s)/flock-pkg-recovered
       git -C ~/sovereign archive <commit>:<path-at-that-commit> \
         | tar -x -C ~/.recovery-archive/<ts>/flock-pkg-recovered/

  3. Read what it was:
       head -1 ~/.recovery-archive/<ts>/flock-pkg-recovered/package.json 2>/dev/null
       head -20 ~/.recovery-archive/<ts>/flock-pkg-recovered/README.md
       rg -n 'flock-pkg' ~/sovereign 2>/dev/null | rg -v '\.git/'

  4. Decide placement. If it is:
       the free-pool provider referenced in the old plan → belongs under
         range/ranch/stockyard/flock — but verify first; flock and
         flock-pkg may be the same thing or flock-pkg may be a package
         wrapper around flock
       a distinct component → its own place under range/ranch/
       dead code → note it, do not restore

  5. Restore with `git checkout <commit> -- <path>` into the correct
     location, then commit.

If flock-pkg cannot be found in git history, note it and continue. Do
not attempt filesystem recovery.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 3 — CLASSIFY EVERYTHING UNDER range/
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

For every directory under range/ and range/ranch/, in order of depth
(leaves first):

  Read:
    manifest    go.mod / package.json / Cargo.toml / pyproject.toml
    README      first paragraph
    entrypoint  main.go / index.ts / server.go

  Record:
    name:       <basename>
    path:       <full path>
    identity:   <module name from manifest, or "no manifest">
    role:       <one line from README+code>
    status:     monorepo | child-component | duplicate-checkout |
                retired-alias | container-wrapper | dead | unknown

  If a directory has the same module identity as another directory
  anywhere under ~/sovereign or ~/projects, both are duplicate-checkout
  and merge into the survivor.

Do not move anything yet. Do not rename anything. Just classify.

Write the classification to /tmp/classification.txt. Every directory
gets a line with evidence (which file you read to determine identity).

Report the classification table before moving to step 4.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 4 — MERGE DUPLICATES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

For every pair (or group) with the same module identity and different
HEADs:

  git -C <survivor> worktree add --detach \
      ~/.recovery-worktrees/merge-<name> <older-HEAD>
  cd ~/.recovery-worktrees/merge-<name>
  git merge --no-commit --no-ff <newer-HEAD>

  For every conflicted file:
    git show :1:<file> > /tmp/base
    git show :2:<file> > /tmp/ours
    git show :3:<file> > /tmp/theirs
    Read all three. Write the file that should exist.

  Commit. Fast-forward survivor. Archive loser.

Known merge candidates to check specifically:

  paddock vs vansrouter vs 9router
    paddock README says it's VansRouter.
    ~/sovereign/projects/vansrouter/ exists.
    ~/sovereign/projects/9router/ exists.
    All three may be the same codebase. Check module identity on each.

  corral vs super-ralph vs ralph
    corral README says "@sovereign/corral (aka ralph)".
    Find every copy of this module across ~/sovereign and ~/projects.

  herd vs llama-swap vs sovereign-swap
    Same codebase, three names. Find every copy, merge into one.

  flock vs flock-pkg
    flock-pkg may be the npm-package version of flock, or distinct.
    Check module identity.

  router vs herd
    range/router/ was moved to ranch/stockyard/router by the previous
    agent. Was range/router the same as herd, or a distinct router?
    Check module identity.

For every merge, write one entry in MERGE-DECISIONS.md at the survivor
root. Format: path / ours / theirs / decision / reason (one sentence).

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 5 — REPAIR THE BROKEN RENAMES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The previous agent used plain mv for the mesh → range rename and for
the moves into ranch/stockyard and ranch/barn. Those need to be
converted to proper git renames so history follows.

For each path the agent moved, check git status:

  If git shows "deleted: <old>" and "untracked: <new>" for the same
  content, repair:

    git -C <repo> rm --cached <old>     # if git thinks <old> is deleted
    git -C <repo> add <new>
    git -C <repo> commit -m "fix: convert mv to git mv for <path>"

  Better: for each moved path, move it back to its old location with
  plain mv, then `git mv <old> <new>`, then commit. That preserves
  rename detection.

Then verify:

  For each moved path:
    git -C ~/sovereign log --follow --oneline -- <new-path> | head -5
    Should show history that predates the move.

Folder renames that still need to happen:

  range/ranch/routers → range/ranch/stockyard    (verify: was it done?)
  range/ranch/mcp     → range/ranch/barn         (verify: was it done?)

If stockyard/ or barn/ were created by plain mv, the git history is
broken. Repair by recreating the rename as a `git mv` from the original
path in a temporary worktree, then replacing.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 6 — MOVE REMAINING CHILDREN INTO THEIR MONOREPOS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

For each child-component still at the range/ top level whose parent is
range/ranch/:

  git -C ~/sovereign mv <old-path> <new-path>
  git -C ~/sovereign commit -m "move <name> under <parent>"

Verify after each move:
  ls -la <new-path>
  git -C ~/sovereign status --short | grep -E '<old>|<new>'
  # should show one rename, not a delete+add

If a move fails with "bad source", the source doesn't exist or the
destination's parent doesn't exist. Check both, then retry.

Do not use plain mv.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

goal.objective:
RECOVERY AND COMPLETION PLAN — range/ranch.

A previous agent executed part of a plan and made mistakes. This plan
starts from the CURRENT state, recovers what was destroyed, finishes
what was started, and verifies the result. Do not re-execute anything
from the old plan.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
WHAT THE PREVIOUS AGENT DID — STARTING STATE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

It renamed ~/sovereign/projects/mesh → ~/sovereign/projects/range using
plain `mv` (not `git mv`). Git history for that rename is broken.

It then ran plain `mv` to move things under range/ranch/:

  corral      → range/ranch/corral
  router      → range/ranch/stockyard/router-legacy, later
                → range/ranch/stockyard/router
  gateway     → range/ranch/barn/gateway
  browserless → range/ranch/barn/browserless
  secretsmith → range/ranch/barn/secretsmith
  gemini-mcp  → range/ranch/barn/gemini-mcp
  ast-matrix  → range/ranch/barn/ast-matrix
  data        → range/ranch/data
  research    → range/ranch/research
  squawk      → range/ranch/squawk
  squawk-ws   → range/ranch/squawk-ws
  flock-pkg   → rm -rf  (DESTROYED, not archived)

It read two READMEs and learned:
  corral   = @sovereign/corral (aka ralph, aka super-ralph)
  paddock  = VansRouter (aka 9router, matches ~/sovereign/projects/vansrouter)

But it did not classify anything else. It did not merge duplicates.
It did not update configs. It did not purge symlinks. It did not verify.

Some of the mv commands may have failed silently. Do not trust the list
above as ground truth. Inventory first.

RECOVERY AND COMPLETION PLAN — range/ranch.

A previous agent executed part of a plan and made mistakes. This plan
starts from the CURRENT state, recovers what was destroyed, finishes
what was started, and verifies the result. Do not re-execute anything
from the old plan.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
WHAT THE PREVIOUS AGENT DID — STARTING STATE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

It renamed ~/sovereign/projects/mesh → ~/sovereign/projects/range using
plain `mv` (not `git mv`). Git history for that rename is broken.

It then ran plain `mv` to move things under range/ranch/:

  corral      → range/ranch/corral
  router      → range/ranch/stockyard/router-legacy, later
                → range/ranch/stockyard/router
  gateway     → range/ranch/barn/gateway
  browserless → range/ranch/barn/browserless
  secretsmith → range/ranch/barn/secretsmith
  gemini-mcp  → range/ranch/barn/gemini-mcp
  ast-matrix  → range/ranch/barn/ast-matrix
  data        → range/ranch/data
  research    → range/ranch/research
  squawk      → range/ranch/squawk
  squawk-ws   → range/ranch/squawk-ws
  flock-pkg   → rm -rf  (DESTROYED, not archived)

It read two READMEs and learned:
  corral   = @sovereign/corral (aka ralph, aka super-ralph)
  paddock  = VansRouter (aka 9router, matches ~/sovereign/projects/vansrouter)

But it did not classify anything else. It did not merge duplicates.
It did not update configs. It did not purge symlinks. It did not verify.

Some of the mv commands may have failed silently. Do not trust the list
above as ground truth. Inventory first.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
HARD RULES FOR THIS PLAN
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. Never `mv`. Always `git mv` inside the containing repo. If `git mv`
   fails with "bad source", the path is wrong or already moved — check
   before doing anything else.

2. Never `rm -rf` anything. If something needs to go, archive first:
     tar czf ~/.recovery-archive/<ts>/<name>.tar.gz <path>/
   Then remove the directory. Keep the archive for the whole session.

3. Before every move, run `git -C <repo> ls-files --error-unmatch <path>`
   to confirm the path is tracked. If it isn't tracked, investigate
   before moving.

4. Before classifying any directory, read its README first paragraph and
   its manifest (go.mod / package.json / Cargo.toml / pyproject.toml).
   Do not assume from the name.

5. Before merging any pair of directories, confirm they share a module
   identity. Same module = same codebase. Different module = do not
   merge regardless of names.

6. Merge conflicts resolved by reading :1:/:2:/:3: and writing the
   correct file. Never -X, --ours, --theirs, --union, git merge-file,
   or conflict markers in output.

7. Never edit ~/.bashrc.

8. If a git operation goes sideways, stop and use gitpanic / gitundo /
   gitfix to diagnose before proceeding.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 1 — FREEZE AND INVENTORY CURRENT STATE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Do not modify anything yet. Read only.

  cd ~/sovereign/projects/range

  fd -t d -H . . --max-depth 4 > /tmp/state-now.txt
  fd -t l -H . . > /tmp/state-symlinks.txt

  git -C ~/sovereign status --short > /tmp/git-status.txt
  git -C ~/sovereign diff --stat --submodule=short > /tmp/git-diff.txt

  # did flock-pkg survive anywhere?
  fd -t d -H 'flock-pkg' ~/sovereign ~/.recovery-archive 2>/dev/null
  git -C ~/sovereign log --all --oneline -- '**/flock-pkg/**' 2>/dev/null

  # unreachable objects from the deletion?
  git -C ~/sovereign fsck --unreachable --no-reflogs 2>/dev/null \
    > /tmp/unreachable.txt
  wc -l /tmp/unreachable.txt

  cat ~/sovereign/.gitmodules

  pgrep -af 'range|mesh|ranch|herd|stockyard|gateway|squawk|secretsmith|vansrouter|9router|corral|paddock'

Read /tmp/state-now.txt. Every directory currently under range/ is a
candidate to classify. Every path the agent moved is a candidate to
find in git history.

Report what you found before moving to step 2.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 2 — RECOVER flock-pkg
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

flock-pkg was deleted with rm -rf. It may still exist in git history.

  1. Find its last commit:
       git -C ~/sovereign log --all --oneline -- '**/flock-pkg/**'

  2. If a commit is found, restore to a staging area:
       mkdir -p ~/.recovery-archive/$(date +%s)/flock-pkg-recovered
       git -C ~/sovereign archive <commit>:<path-at-that-commit> \
         | tar -x -C ~/.recovery-archive/<ts>/flock-pkg-recovered/

  3. Read what it was:
       head -1 ~/.recovery-archive/<ts>/flock-pkg-recovered/package.json 2>/dev/null
       head -20 ~/.recovery-archive/<ts>/flock-pkg-recovered/README.md
       rg -n 'flock-pkg' ~/sovereign 2>/dev/null | rg -v '\.git/'

  4. Decide placement. If it is:
       the free-pool provider referenced in the old plan → belongs under
         range/ranch/stockyard/flock — but verify first; flock and
         flock-pkg may be the same thing or flock-pkg may be a package
         wrapper around flock
       a distinct component → its own place under range/ranch/
       dead code → note it, do not restore

  5. Restore with `git checkout <commit> -- <path>` into the correct
     location, then commit.

If flock-pkg cannot be found in git history, note it and continue. Do
not attempt filesystem recovery.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 3 — CLASSIFY EVERYTHING UNDER range/
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

For every directory under range/ and range/ranch/, in order of depth
(leaves first):

  Read:
    manifest    go.mod / package.json / Cargo.toml / pyproject.toml
    README      first paragraph
    entrypoint  main.go / index.ts / server.go

  Record:
    name:       <basename>
    path:       <full path>
    identity:   <module name from manifest, or "no manifest">
    role:       <one line from README+code>
    status:     monorepo | child-component | duplicate-checkout |
                retired-alias | container-wrapper | dead | unknown

  If a directory has the same module identity as another directory
  anywhere under ~/sovereign or ~/projects, both are duplicate-checkout
  and merge into the survivor.

Do not move anything yet. Do not rename anything. Just classify.

Write the classification to /tmp/classification.txt. Every directory
gets a line with evidence (which file you read to determine identity).

Report the classification table before moving to step 4.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 4 — MERGE DUPLICATES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

For every pair (or group) with the same module identity and different
HEADs:

  git -C <survivor> worktree add --detach \
      ~/.recovery-worktrees/merge-<name> <older-HEAD>
  cd ~/.recovery-worktrees/merge-<name>
  git merge --no-commit --no-ff <newer-HEAD>

  For every conflicted file:
    git show :1:<file> > /tmp/base
    git show :2:<file> > /tmp/ours
    git show :3:<file> > /tmp/theirs
    Read all three. Write the file that should exist.

  Commit. Fast-forward survivor. Archive loser.

Known merge candidates to check specifically:

  paddock vs vansrouter vs 9router
    paddock README says it's VansRouter.
    ~/sovereign/projects/vansrouter/ exists.
    ~/sovereign/projects/9router/ exists.
    All three may be the same codebase. Check module identity on each.

  corral vs super-ralph vs ralph
    corral README says "@sovereign/corral (aka ralph)".
    Find every copy of this module across ~/sovereign and ~/projects.

  herd vs llama-swap vs sovereign-swap
    Same codebase, three names. Find every copy, merge into one.

  flock vs flock-pkg
    flock-pkg may be the npm-package version of flock, or distinct.
    Check module identity.

  router vs herd
    range/router/ was moved to ranch/stockyard/router by the previous
    agent. Was range/router the same as herd, or a distinct router?
    Check module identity.

For every merge, write one entry in MERGE-DECISIONS.md at the survivor
root. Format: path / ours / theirs / decision / reason (one sentence).

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 5 — REPAIR THE BROKEN RENAMES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The previous agent used plain mv for the mesh → range rename and for
the moves into ranch/stockyard and ranch/barn. Those need to be
converted to proper git renames so history follows.

For each path the agent moved, check git status:

  If git shows "deleted: <old>" and "untracked: <new>" for the same
  content, repair:

    git -C <repo> rm --cached <old>     # if git thinks <old> is deleted
    git -C <repo> add <new>
    git -C <repo> commit -m "fix: convert mv to git mv for <path>"

  Better: for each moved path, move it back to its old location with
  plain mv, then `git mv <old> <new>`, then commit. That preserves
  rename detection.

Then verify:

  For each moved path:
    git -C ~/sovereign log --follow --oneline -- <new-path> | head -5
    Should show history that predates the move.

Folder renames that still need to happen:

  range/ranch/routers → range/ranch/stockyard    (verify: was it done?)
  range/ranch/mcp     → range/ranch/barn         (verify: was it done?)

If stockyard/ or barn/ were created by plain mv, the git history is
broken. Repair by recreating the rename as a `git mv` from the original
path in a temporary worktree, then replacing.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 6 — MOVE REMAINING CHILDREN INTO THEIR MONOREPOS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

For each child-component still at the range/ top level whose parent is
range/ranch/:

  git -C ~/sovereign mv <old-path> <new-path>
  git -C ~/sovereign commit -m "move <name> under <parent>"

Verify after each move:
  ls -la <new-path>
  git -C ~/sovereign status --short | grep -E '<old>|<new>'
  # should show one rename, not a delete+add

If a move fails with "bad source", the source doesn't exist or the
destination's parent doesn't exist. Check both, then retry.

Do not use plain mv.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 7 — CONFIG REWRITE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

For every path that moved, update every config that referenced the old
path. Use rg to find references, then edit each by hand (or with sd
after reading).

Files to update:
  ~/sovereign/pitchfork.toml
  ~/sovereign/mise.toml
  ~/sovereign/stack/services/*.sh
  ~/sovereign/config/*
  ~/sovereign/.gitmodules
  ~/.config/systemd/user/*.service  *.path  *.socket
  ~/.config/environment.d/*
  ~/.local/bin/* launchers
  ~/.bashrc.env (only if it references moved paths — commit dotfiles)
  ~/.agent/*

Retired strings to eliminate from paths and configs (except where
externally required):

  /mesh/
  super-ralph (as a path)
  llama-swap (as a path or service name)
  sovereign-swap (as a path)
  /routers/ (as a path segment under ranch)
  /mcp/ (as a path segment under ranch)

After the rewrite:

  rg -n 'projects/mesh|projects/range/ranch/routers|projects/range/ranch/mcp' \
     ~/sovereign ~/projects ~/.config ~/.local/bin 2>/dev/null

Zero hits, or the remaining hits have inline comments saying
"# required by <external thing>, do not rename".

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 8 — SYMLINK PURGE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

  fd -t l -H . ~/sovereign ~/projects > /tmp/symlinks.txt

For each symlink:
  readlink -f it.
  If the target no longer exists, the symlink is broken by the moves.
    Find every reference to the symlink path.
    Update the references to the canonical path directly.
    Delete the symlink.
  If the target exists and is canonical, same treatment: update
  callers, then delete the symlink.
  Loop until /tmp/symlinks.txt shows zero under ~/sovereign and
  ~/projects (excluding git internals and OS-managed systemd wants).

  Pay special attention to symlinks whose target was under mesh/. They
  all broke when mesh was renamed. Many reference things the previous
  agent then moved again.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STEP 9 — BUILD, RUN, VERIFY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

For every Go module touched:
  go build ./... && go test ./... && go vet ./...

For every other language module: its equivalent.

For the router (herd):
  ./<router-binary> --validate -config ~/sovereign/config/herd.yaml
  mise -C ~/sovereign run restart-herd
  curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:25100/health
  curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:25100/v1/models | jq '.data | length'

Assertions (all must be zero):
  fd -t l -H . ~/sovereign ~/projects | wc -l
  rg -c 'projects/mesh' ~/sovereign ~/projects 2>/dev/null | wc -l
  rg -c 'ranch/routers|ranch/mcp' ~/sovereign ~/projects 2>/dev/null | wc -l
  rg -c '^<<<<<<<|^=======|^>>>>>>>' ~/sovereign ~/projects 2>/dev/null | wc -l

# tmux-mcp v2.0

MCP server for tmux session inspection and control. Hardened for multi-socket estates.

## Tools

| Tool | Access | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `tmux_list` | Read-only | Lists sessions across **all** discovered tmux sockets (default + named like `tauhyperfix`) |
| `tmux_capture` | Read-only | Captures pane scrollback (last 100 lines). `target` like `session:window.pane`, optional `socket` |
| `tmux_send` | **Destructive-gated** | Sends keys to a pane. Requires explicit `confirm:true` — refused otherwise |

## Socket discovery

Scans `/tmp/tmux-<uid>/` (or `$TMUX_TMPDIR`) for socket files. The default socket plus any named sockets (e.g. `tauhyperfix`) are enumerated. The old v1 only saw the default socket.

## Destructive-send gating

`tmux_send` is never accidental: the schema requires `confirm:true`, and the server logs every confirmed send to stderr. Never send to interactive shells without the user's informed intent.

## Running

```bash
/home/toxic/.bun/bin/bun /home/toxic/sovereign/tools/tmux-mcp/server.ts
```

Registered in the mesh gateway (`mesh/gateway/mcp_config.json`) as `tmux` (currently disabled pending deployment review).

- [Fleet Knowledgebase](../../docs/fleet-knowledgebase.md) — crew `tau-tmux-mcp`

# websearch-mcp

Stdlib-only MCP wrapper for the `websearch-skill` CLI package (v0.6.1).

## Why

`websearch-skill` 0.6.1 ships no MCP server — it's CLI-only. This wrapper exposes its capabilities over MCP stdio using only the Python standard library (no extra dependencies).

## Tools

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `web_search` | Web search via `websearch web-search --json` |
| `web_fetch` | Fetch a URL via `websearch web-fetch --json` |
| `arxiv_search` | arXiv search |
| `github_search` | GitHub code/repo search |

## Running

```bash
python3 /home/toxic/sovereign/tools/websearch-mcp/server.py
```

Requires the `websearch` CLI on PATH (`uvx websearch-skill` provides it).

## Verification

Live-tested 2026-09-20: initialize + tools/list + real `web_search` for "Model Context Protocol" returned live Wikipedia results.

## See also

- [Fleet Knowledgebase](../../docs/fleet-knowledgebase.md) — crew `tau-tmux-mcp`
- [Mesh gateway](../../projects/mesh/gateway/) — registered as `websearch-mcp`

the first production consumer of this browserless service needed a supervised,
token-gated headless browser on the mesh. That is why the pitchfork daemon was

# browser-keeper

One persistent headed Chromium for the whole mesh. First-class citizen of
browserless-mcp: MCP tasks drive it through `persistent_*` tools instead of
spawning ephemeral sessions, so logins, tabs and state survive across tasks.

## Layout

- `keeper.js` - the daemon. Owns `/home/toxic/.browserless/profiles/nv-audit`
  exclusively, exposes CDP on `127.0.0.1:9223`, writes
  `/home/toxic/.browserless/keeper/status.json`, relaunches Chromium if it
  dies. Single-instance: exits if CDP already answers.

# Browserless — sovereign mesh

Browser automation for the fleet: the **browserless.io MCP server** plus the
**native-launcher deployment** of the browserless server itself, unified
in one mesh project at `projects/mesh/browserless/` (visible as `mesh/browserless/`).

## Topology (the real serve path)

Two separate lanes — do not confuse them:

```text
browser-keeper daemon (pitchfork: browser-keeper)
  └─ headed Chromium, nv-audit profile ── CDP 127.0.0.1:9223
       └─ browserless-mcp persistent_* tools (11: status/tabs/new_tab/
          close_tab/activate_tab/navigate/screenshot/click/fill/text/evaluate)
            └─ stdio ── ./mcp.sh ── mesh MCP registry (browserless-mcp)

vendor browserless.io v2.49.0 app (/home/toxic/.browserless/app, stock, untouched)
  └─ HTTP 127.0.0.1:25130 (pitchfork: browserless)
       └─ browserless-mcp legacy HTTP tools (initialize_browserless + 14 more)
            └─ stdio ── ./mcp.sh ── mesh MCP registry (browserless-mcp)
```

The MCP server is **stdio only** — no port, no daemon. MCP clients spawn
`./mcp.sh` per session, and it **refuses to start** if the keeper CDP is

     tar czf ~/.recovery-archive/<ts>/<name>.tar.gz <path>/

3. Before every move, run `git -C <repo> ls-files --error-unmatch <path>`
   to confirm the path is tracked. If it isn't tracked, investigate
   before moving.

   its manifest (go.mod / package.json / Cargo.toml / pyproject.toml).
   Do not assume from the name.

5. Before merging any pair of directories, confirm they share a module
   identity. Same module = same codebase. Different module = do not
   merge regardless of names.

6. Merge conflicts resolved by reading :1:/:2:/:3: and writing the
   correct file. Never -X, --ours, --theirs, --union, git merge-file,
   or conflict markers in output.

7. Never edit ~/.bashrc.

8. If a git operation goes sideways, stop and use gitpanic / gitundo /
   gitfix to diagnose before proceeding.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# herd (llama-swap) loopback launcher — binds Go binary to 127.0.0.1:HERD_PORT (25100).
# Renamed from llama-swap.sh — project-wide herd naming, llama-swap binary kept for compatibility.
# No proxy/middleware hop. mesh-hub (25115) serves 20 GHAS /mesh/* features.
# Config: --config <main> plus --config-dir /home/toxic/kimi-auto/herd.d
# (additive, watch-config hot-reload) for the kimi-auto virtual model.
# Lifecycle is owned by pitchfork (supervisor); this script does NOT kill or
# steal the port — if the bind fails, pitchfork sees the failure and retries.
set -euo pipefail
SOV="$HOME/sovereign"
source "$SOV/stack/lib-ports.sh"
require_env HERD_PORT
# Canonical secrets for provider keyEnvs (FLOCK_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, ...).
# Sourced, never copied — keys stay in /home/toxic/.secrets.
if [[ -f /home/toxic/.secrets ]]; then
  set -a
  set +u  # .secrets has forward refs (e.g. ${NVIDIA_API_KEY}); don't crash
  source /home/toxic/.secrets
  set -u
  set +a
fi
PORT="$HERD_PORT"
BIN="$HOME/sovereign/projects/herd/llama-swap"
[[ -x "$BIN" ]] || { echo "herd (llama-swap) bin not found at $BIN" >&2; exit 1; }
CONF="$SOV/config/herd.yaml"
[[ -f "$CONF" ]] || CONF="$SOV/config/llama-swap.yaml"
[[ -f "$CONF" ]] || { echo "herd config not found at $CONF" >&2; exit 1; }

# Launch Go binary — loopback bind only (no 0.0.0.0 exposure).
# exec replaces this shell so the supervisor tracks the ACTUAL server PID,
# not a bash wrapper (2026-09-18: fixes stale-ownership where wrapper PID
# != server PID). pitchfork ready_http gates on /health; no background+wait.
exec "$BIN" --config "$CONF" --config-dir /home/toxic/kimi-auto/herd.d --watch-config --listen "127.0.0.1:${PORT}"

It then ran plain `mv` to move things under range/ranch/:

  corral      → range/ranch/corral
  router      → range/ranch/stockyard/router-legacy, later
                → range/ranch/stockyard/router

HARD RULES FOR THIS PLAN
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. Never `mv`. Always `git mv` inside the containing repo. If `git mv`
   fails with "bad source", the path is wrong or already moved — check
   before doing anything else.

2. Never `rm -rf` anything. If something needs to go, archive first:
     tar czf ~/.recovery-archive/<ts>/<name>.tar.gz <path>/
   Then remove the directory. Keep the archive for the whole session.

3. Before every move, run `git -C <repo> ls-files --error-unmatch <path>`
   to confirm the path is tracked. If it isn't tracked, investigate
   before moving.

4. Before classifying any directory, read its README first paragraph and
   its manifest (go.mod / package.json / Cargo.toml / pyproject.toml).
   Do not assume from the name.

5. Before merging any pair of directories, confirm they share a module
   identity. Same module = same codebase. Different module = do not
   merge regardless of names.

6. Merge conflicts resolved by reading :1:/:2:/:3: and writing the
   correct file. Never -X, --ours, --theirs, --union, git merge-file,
   or conflict markers in output.

7. Never edit ~/.bashrc.

8. If a git operation goes sideways, stop and use gitpanic / gitundo /
   gitfix to diagnose before proceeding.
